title: Microsoft Teams: attendee chat in town halls for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, policy controls, licensing and documented chat limitations are supported. It explicitly distinguishes commercial behaviour from the planned government release and reports Microsoft's conflicting availability and policy-default documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans public event chat between all users in events larger than 1,000 users or any event optimised for a large audience.
claims.quote: All users in Events larger than 1,000 users or in any Event optimized for a large audience can now chat with one another in a public event chat in GCC, GCC High and DoD.

claims.claim: Large-audience attendee chat messages are stored only in the organiser's mailbox, excluding the separate event group chat.

claims.quote: Meeting chat messages in events optimized for large audiences, excluding the event group chat, are stored only in an organizer's mailbox for up to 30 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft's event chat page says placing the organiser's mailbox on legal hold keeps these chat messages longer.
claims.quote: However, if you place the organizer’s mailbox on legal hold, the mailbox keeps the chat messages for longer.

claims.claim: TeamsEventsPolicy is a user-level policy for tenant administrators, with the chat permission applying to the organiser.
claims.quote:
User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences.
This setting governs whether the user can enable the Comment Stream chat experience for an event optimized for a large audience.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference describes the policy as currently still in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows you to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Note that this policy is currently still in preview.

claims.claim: The chat permission is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience chat experience.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**.
Select the policy you want to edit or create a new one.
In the **Events optimized for a large audience chat experience** dropdown list, select **Optimized** (the default value) or **None**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None turns off the organiser's ability to enable attendee chat.
claims.quote:
To turn off chat for attendees in events optimized for large audiences, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallChatExperience None

claims.claim: None prevents organisers from turning on attendee chat, while Optimized allows them to do so.
claims.quote:
| Optimized | **This is the default value.** Organizers with this policy can turn on chat for their attendees. |
| None | Organizers with this policy can't turn on chat for their attendees. |

claims.claim: Attendance restrictions are at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
For events [optimized for large audiences](plan-events), such as town halls, in the **Who can attend events optimized for a large audience**dropdown list

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests restricts attendance to the organisation and guests.
claims.quote:
To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The attendance setting defaults to Everyone, permitting any user to attend, including people outside the organisation.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to **Everyone**. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.claim: The attendance policy documents EveryoneInOrganization and EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests as alternatives to Everyone.
claims.quote: `-TownhallEventAttendeeAccess`(Everyone,EveryoneInOrganization,EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests)

claims.claim: Town hall creation is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Events policies**.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
For events [optimized for large audiences](plan-events), such as town halls, turn the **Events optimized for a large audience** toggle **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating large-audience events.
claims.quote:
To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Turning off event creation after an event has been scheduled prevents its organiser from running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to **Off** after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.
